# Observation feed + telemetry: current flow digest

## What it is
Two loosely-coupled telemetry layers share this digest because both move numbers out of the data plane and into observers. (1) The **observation Feed** (`internal/core/observation`) is an in-process, typed, multi-subscriber pub/sub bus: the trafficusage eBPF collector and the flowexport conntrack worker publish per-source-IP and per-flow byte observations onto it; `trafficstat` and `trafficfeature` each subscribe independently and maintain their own lazy, consumer-refcounted aggregation. `internal/core/stats` supplies the allocation-light primitives (rolling window, EWMA, entropy, interval regularity) both aggregators build on. (2) The **metrics/telemetry stack** (`internal/core/metrics`, `internal/component/telemetry`) is an always-on `Registry` interface that any component records into, exposed by an optional Netdata-compatible OS collector set and a Prometheus HTTP exporter, both gated behind the `ze_telemetry` build tag. **gNMI** (`internal/component/gnmi`) is a third, independent exporter: it streams the YANG config/state tree over gRPC and never touches the metrics registry or the observation Feed except to record its own RPC counters. All three fan-out mechanisms (Feed, iface tick, gNMI Subscribe) use the same copy-on-write-snapshot-plus-drop-on-full idiom, but each is a separate implementation.

## Flow
1. **Producer 1: trafficusage eBPF.** `Monitor.poll` (`internal/plugins/trafficusage/monitor.go:251`) runs on the monitor's own 1s poller (`pollLoop`, `internal/plugins/trafficusage/monitor.go:230`, started by `runEngine`, `internal/plugins/trafficusage/register.go:82`) and calls `publishLocked` (`internal/plugins/trafficusage/monitor.go:289`), which sets Prometheus gauges from cumulative BPF-map byte counters and, for every tracked source IP, builds `observation.Observation{Kind: KindSourceIP, Feature: FeatureRxBytes, Value: <cumulative bytes>}` and calls `feed.Publish(obs)` (`internal/plugins/trafficusage/monitor.go:294`, `internal/plugins/trafficusage/monitor.go:323`, `internal/plugins/trafficusage/monitor.go:331`). This poller is independent of the iface 1Hz tick (step 8) even though both default to 1s.
2. **Producer 2: flowexport conntrack.** The conntrack worker computes per-flow byte/packet deltas since the last dump via `DeltaTracker` (`internal/plugins/flowexport/conntrack_worker.go:145`, `internal/plugins/flowexport/conntrack_worker.go:198`) and calls `exporter.exportFlows` (`internal/plugins/flowexport/exporter.go:246`), which enriches and rings the flows, then for each flow builds `observation.Observation{Kind: KindFlow, Feature: FeatureFlowBytes, Value: <delta bytes>}` and calls `feed.Publish(obs)` (`internal/plugins/flowexport/exporter.go:308`, `internal/plugins/flowexport/exporter.go:311`, `internal/plugins/flowexport/exporter.go:322`). Unlike trafficusage's cumulative counters, these values are deltas (`plan/learned/1016-observation-feed.md`).
3. **Feed.Publish is the fan-out core.** `Publish` (`observation.go:180`) loads the current `atomic.Pointer[subscriberSnapshot]` and, for every subscriber, attempts a non-blocking send on that subscriber's own cap-1024 buffered channel (`observation.go:184`); a full channel drops the observation and bumps both an internal counter and (if bound) the `ze_observation_dropped_total` Prometheus counter. The publisher's goroutine never blocks and never touches subscriber state directly.
4. **Each subscriber drains on its own goroutine.** `Feed.Subscribe` (`observation.go:105`) creates the channel/quit/done triple and spawns `subscriber.drain` (`observation.go:135`), which loops `select` over the channel (calling `fn(obs)`) and a `quit` signal. `Unsubscribe` (`observation.go:150`) is copy-on-write like `Subscribe`: it builds a new snapshot slice without the removed entry, atomically stores it, then closes `quit` and blocks on `done` so the caller's detach is synchronous with the drain goroutine's exit, the data channel itself is left open (not `close`d) so a concurrent `Publish` still holding the stale snapshot never sends on a closed channel.
5. **Two real Feed subscribers, different filters, different ingestion.** `internal/component/trafficstat.Service.start` subscribes as `"trafficstat"` (`internal/component/trafficstat/service.go:248`) and its `aggregator.ingest` (`internal/component/trafficstat/window.go:60`) switches on `obs.Kind`: `KindSourceIP` calls `a.cumulative` (`internal/component/trafficstat/window.go:88`), which folds the value in via `stats.Window.AddCumulative` (`window.go:43`, the "subtract from last cumulative sample" path, since trafficusage's value is a running counter); `KindFlow` calls `a.delta` (`internal/component/trafficstat/window.go:101`), which uses `stats.Window.AddDelta` (`window.go:34`, add-as-is, since flowexport's value is already a per-publish delta). `trafficfeature.Service.start` subscribes as `"trafficfeature"` (`service.go:164`) and its `aggregator.ingest` (`feature.go:102`) is deliberately narrower: it discards everything except `Kind==KindFlow && Feature==FeatureFlowBytes` and only ever calls `AddDelta` (`feature.go:116`, `feature.go:131`), because it never sees a cumulative source.
6. **Both aggregators are lazy, consumer-refcounted.** Neither subscribes to the Feed until `Attach()` (`service.go:113`; trafficstat's equivalent at `internal/component/trafficstat/service.go:134`) takes the consumer count 0->1 and calls `start()` (`service.go:158`); `Detach()` (`service.go:131`) calls `stop()` (`service.go:174`) on the 1->0 transition, which unsubscribes from the Feed (`s.feed.Unsubscribe(s.feedSubID)`, `service.go:181`) and stops the tick goroutine. No consumer attached means zero Feed fan-out work for that subscriber.
7. **Per-tick finalize.** A 1s ticker (`tickInterval`, `service.go:25`) drives `run` -> `tick()` (`service.go:186`, `service.go:202`), which calls `aggregator.snapshot(now)` (`feature.go:141`; trafficstat's at `internal/component/trafficstat/window.go:149`). `snapshot` closes the current window via `stats.Window.Tick(dt)` (`window.go:55`), computes derived features, `FanOut` (distinct destinations), `OutInRatio`, `stats.Entropy` for `PortEntropy` (`entropy.go:11`), `stats.IntervalRegularity` for `Beaconing` (`beacon.go:19`), evicts entities idle past `evictIdleTicks`, and the result is atomically stored as the latest snapshot (`s.snap.Store(...)`, `service.go:209`).
8. **Consumers read the snapshot, not the Feed.** `show traffic feature` (`internal/component/trafficfeature/cmd/traffic_feature.go:26`) calls `EnsureGlobal()` -> `Attach()` -> `Snapshot()` (`service.go:150`, a lock-free `atomic.Pointer` load) -> `Detach()`, converting the result to a `plugin.Map` (`snapshotToMap`, `traffic_feature.go:48`). The anomaly detector (`internal/plugins/anomaly/detect/detector.go:120`, `onTick`) is the second consumer of `trafficfeature.Snapshot`; the ddos detector instead consumes `trafficstat`'s own aggregated output via a second-order fan-out, `trafficstat.Service.SubscribeRates` (`internal/component/trafficstat/service.go:185`). Both judgment layers are beyond this digest; it stops at the neutral-feature boundary.
9. **A second, older, synchronous fan-out: the iface 1Hz tick.** Independent of the Feed, `internal/component/iface/rate.go`'s `rateTracker.collect` (`internal/component/iface/rate.go:183`) runs on its own 1s ticker and, after updating its own Prometheus gauges, calls every `SubscribeCollectNotify` subscriber **in-line, on the ticker goroutine** (`internal/component/iface/rate.go:240-244`), not via a buffered channel. trafficusage's `mon.onSnapshot` (attach/detach lifecycle only, not a Feed publish) and flowexport's `notifyFromRateTracker` both register here (`internal/plugins/trafficusage/register.go:78`, `internal/plugins/flowexport/register.go:112`). A slow subscriber on this path stalls the rate tracker's own tick; the deprecated single-callback `RegisterCollectNotify` (`internal/component/iface/rate.go:121`) still exists as a compatibility wrapper over the same copy-on-write subscriber list. Both trafficusage and flowexport declare `Dependencies: []string{"interface"}` in their own `registry.Registration` (`internal/plugins/trafficusage/register.go:27`, `internal/plugins/flowexport/register.go:69`), so configuring either plugin alone is sufficient to also start the iface component and its rate tracker; without that declared dependency, `SubscribeCollectNotify` would register into a list nobody ever ticks.
10. **Metrics registry: always-on collection, optional exposure.** Any component gets a `metrics.Registry` (`Counter`/`Gauge`/`CounterVec`/`GaugeVec`/`Histogram`/`HistogramVec`, `core/metrics/metrics.go:57`) via `registry.GetMetricsRegistry()` (`internal/component/plugin/registry/registry.go:368`) or a `ConfigureMetrics(reg)` callback wired at plugin registration (e.g. `internal/component/iface/register.go:146-148` calls both `bindMetricsRegistry(reg)` and `observation.BindMetrics(reg)`, which is how the Feed's own `ze_observation_*` counters get bound). Every `BindMetrics` nil-guards (`if reg == nil { return }`, `observation.go:24`, `service.go:68`) so metrics stay optional without a `NopRegistry` indirection; other plugin families (OSPF, ISIS) instead seed a `metrics.NopRegistry{}` default, two coexisting patterns for the same "registry may be absent" problem. Concretely, trafficusage registers `ze_traffic_usage_ingress_bytes_total`/`ze_traffic_usage_egress_port_bytes_total`/etc. (`internal/plugins/trafficusage/metrics.go:35-39`) and flowexport registers `ze_flowexport_datagrams_total`/`ze_flowexport_bytes_total`/etc. (`internal/plugins/flowexport/metrics.go:30-34`) unconditionally at plugin start; those gauges/counters update every tick whether or not `ze_telemetry` is even compiled in, they simply have no `/metrics` listener to be scraped from without it.
11. **Wiring differs by package: no shared plugin lifecycle across this digest's scope.** Unlike `trafficusage`/`flowexport`/`iface` (each a `registry.Registration` with `RunEngine`, discovered by the plugin manager), none of `trafficfeature`, `trafficstat`, the telemetry exporter, or gnmi register that way. `trafficfeature`/`trafficstat` are bare libraries with a process-wide singleton reached via `EnsureGlobal()` (`internal/component/trafficfeature/register.go:14`); only their `cmd` show-handler subpackages register an RPC (`traffic_feature.go:17`, unconditionally blank-imported by `internal/component/plugin/all/all.go:119`). The telemetry exporter is reached via the `metrics.StartExporter` function-pointer seam (next step), its YANG schema blank-imported only under the `ze_telemetry` tag (`internal/component/plugin/all/all_ze_telemetry.go:10`). gNMI goes further: the WHOLE package, not just its YANG schema, is blank-imported only under `ze_gnmi` (`internal/component/plugin/all/all_ze_gnmi.go:10-12`), and is built and `Serve`d directly by `cmd/ze/hub/service_gnmi.go` (also `//go:build ze_gnmi`) rather than through any plugin lifecycle hook.
12. **The registry is created by the gated HTTP-exporter seam, from either of two call sites.** `metrics.StartExporter` (`exporter_hook.go:31`) is `nil` unless the `ze_telemetry` build tag links `cmd/ze/hub/register_telemetry.go`, whose `init()` sets it to `exporter.Start` (`internal/component/telemetry/exporter/exporter.go:27`). The bgp-reactor config loader calls the seam when `bgp{}` is configured (`internal/component/bgp/config/loader_create.go:202-205`): it creates a `metrics.PrometheusRegistry` (`prometheus.go:35`) inside `Start`, starts the Prometheus HTTP server (`exporter/server.go:104`) and, if `netdata.enabled`, the OS collector manager (`collector.StartOSCollectors`, `collector.go:163`); the loader then hands the SAME registry to both `r.SetMetricsRegistry(reg)` (the BGP reactor) and `registry.SetMetricsRegistry(reg)` (the process-wide plugin-injection slot, `internal/component/plugin/registry/registry.go:361`). The standalone hub path takes the second, mirror route when `telemetry{}` is configured but `bgp{}` is absent: `startStandaloneTelemetry` (`cmd/ze/hub/main_system.go:330`, called from `cmd/ze/hub/main.go:634`) calls the identical seam and only calls `registry.SetMetricsRegistry(reg)` (there is no reactor to also inject into). Either way it is one registry, one owner of `SetMetricsRegistry`; external plugin processes receive it via `process.Manager.SetMetricsRegistry` (`internal/component/plugin/manager/manager.go:165`, warning instead of injecting on a `metrics.Registry` type mismatch, `internal/component/plugin/manager/manager.go:167-168`).
13. **Netdata-compatible OS collectors ride the same registry.** `collector.Manager.Start` (`collector.go:93`) calls `Init(reg, prefix)` once per enabled collector, then `collectAll` (`collector.go:144`) ticks `Collect()` at a per-collector interval (global default, overridable via YANG). `registerPlatformCollectors` (`internal/component/telemetry/collector/platform_linux.go:9`) registers ~30 procfs/sysfs readers (CPU, memory, net, disk, conntrack, SCTP, ZFS, btrfs, wireless, ...) producing Netdata-name-compatible gauges (`netdata_{context}_{units}_average`) into the identical `PrometheusRegistry` that BGP and observation-feed metrics also populate, one `/metrics` endpoint for everything. Concretely, `cpuCollector.Init` (`internal/component/telemetry/collector/cpu_linux.go:34`) registers `{prefix}_system_cpu_percentage_average`/`{prefix}_cpu_cpu_percentage_average`; `conntrackCollector.Init` (`internal/component/telemetry/collector/conntrack_linux.go:65`) registers `{prefix}_netfilter_conntrack_sockets_active_connections_average` among others, the naming, unit-sanitization (`%`->`_percent`, `/s`->`_persec`), and chart/dimension/family labels all mirror Netdata's C source exactly, verified metric-by-metric (`plan/learned/653-netdata-os-collectors.md`), not derived from Netdata's documentation.
14. **HTTP exposure.** `server.start` (`exporter/server.go:104`) mounts `registry.Handler()` (`prometheus.go:224`, `promhttp.HandlerFor`) at `cfg.Path` (default `/metrics`) plus, on the same mux, `internal/core/health.DefaultRegistry.Handler()` (`exporter/server.go:119`, `internal/core/health/registry.go:103`) at `/health`, one process-wide health-check report served from the same listener set, optionally behind HTTP Basic Auth (`basicAuthMiddleware`, `exporter/server.go:194`). Bind is all-or-nothing: a failure on any configured endpoint rolls back listeners already bound (`exporter/server.go:136-146`) rather than serving a partial set.
15. **Config extraction gates everything.** `extractTelemetryConfig` (`exporter/server.go:228`) requires `telemetry.prometheus.enabled == "true"` explicitly (`exporter/server.go:244`, no implicit-enable); `extractNetdataConfig` (`exporter/server.go:312`) defaults the Netdata OS-collector sub-block to enabled with `netdata`/`1s` interval (`defaultNetdataConfig`, `exporter/server.go:355`) but still requires the parent Prometheus block to be enabled first. Settings moved from `telemetry.prometheus.{prefix,interval,collector}` to the nested `netdata` container are still read at the old path for compatibility, only logged as deprecated (`deprecatedNetdataAliases`, `exporter/server.go:364`), never rejected.
16. **gNMI is a fully separate exporter surface.** `gnmi.Server.Get` (`get.go:20`) and `Subscribe` read only the YANG config/state `Tree` via the injected `tree()` accessor, never the metrics `Registry` or the observation `Feed`. Its own RPC counters (`ze_gnmi_requests_total`, `ze_gnmi_errors_total`, `ze_gnmi_subscribe_active`, `initGNMIMetrics`, `gnmi/metrics.go:16`) are the only place gNMI touches the metrics registry, wired via `Server.SetMetricsRegistry` (`gnmi/server.go:123`) called from `cmd/ze/hub/service_gnmi.go:115-116` using `registry.GetMetricsRegistry()`. `Capabilities` (`capabilities.go:14`) is the fourth RPC, advertising the loaded YANG module set (`loadModels`, `capabilities.go:27`, memoized behind a `sync.Once`) and supported encodings; like `Get`/`Set`, it never touches metrics or the Feed either.
17. **gNMI Set commits, then broadcasts.** `Server.Set` (`set.go:25`) opens a `ConfigSessionManager` session (`s.sessions.Enter`, `set.go:41`), applies every delete/replace/update into it (`applyUpdate`, `set.go:119`), then calls `s.sessions.Commit` (`set.go:97`); any failure at any step discards the session (`discardSession`, `set.go:162`) so a `SetRequest` is all-or-nothing. Only on a successful commit does `notifySetResults` (`set.go:170`) call `ChangeNotifier.Notify` (`subscribe.go:62`) once per changed path. Config commits from non-gNMI sources (web, CLI, managed) instead call the coarser `NotifyConfigReload` (`subscribe.go:78`, the only production caller is `cmd/ze/hub/service_gnmi.go:134`), which pushes one generic "config-reload" notification so STREAM subscribers know to re-`Get`. The per-path `NotifyChange` helper (`subscribe.go:89`) exists and is unit-tested (`subscribe_test.go:90`) but has no production caller today, granular ON_CHANGE-style diffing is not yet wired in.
18. **gNMI auth is bearer-token, checked per RPC.** When `Config.Token` is set, `Serve` (`gnmi/server.go:130`) installs `authUnaryInterceptor`/`authStreamInterceptor` (`gnmi/server.go:206`, `gnmi/server.go:214`) ahead of every RPC; `checkAuth` (`gnmi/server.go:227`) extracts the `authorization` metadata, requires a `"Bearer "` prefix, and compares via `sha256`+`subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` (`gnmi/server.go:243-246`) rather than a plain string equality, to avoid a timing side-channel. TLS is independent and optional: `Serve` builds a `tls.Config` from `CertPEM`/`KeyPEM` only when both are non-empty (`gnmi/server.go:140-148`); an empty token or empty cert pair simply skips that layer rather than failing closed.
19. **gNMI `Subscribe` fan-out mirrors the Feed's shape, independently.** `ChangeNotifier.Subscribe` (`subscribe.go:37`) hands back a client channel (cap `subscribeSendBuffer = 32`, `subscribe.go:20`) up to `maxSubscribeClients = 64` (`subscribe.go:19`); `Notify` (`subscribe.go:62`) does the identical non-blocking-send-or-drop as `Feed.Publish`, logging a warning instead of incrementing a Prometheus counter on drop. It is a separate `map[chan]struct{}` under its own `sync.RWMutex`, not a reuse of `observation.Feed` or its copy-on-write snapshot.

## Invariants & gotchas
- **Non-blocking publish, bounded per-subscriber buffer.** `Feed.Publish` never blocks the producer's goroutine (trafficusage's poller, flowexport's conntrack worker); a slow or stuck subscriber only drops its own observations (cap-1024 channel, `observation.go:71`) and increments a drop counter. It never backs up into other subscribers or the publisher.
- **Copy-on-write subscriber list, not a mutex-protected slice.** `Subscribe`/`Unsubscribe` build a whole new `subscriberSnapshot` slice under `f.mu` and atomically swap the pointer (`observation.go:122`, `observation.go:128`, `observation.go:165`); `Publish` reads the pointer once per call with zero locking and zero per-publish allocation. `Unsubscribe` deliberately does not close the data channel (only `quit`), because a concurrent `Publish` may still hold the old snapshot and would panic sending on a closed channel.
- **`Observation` is a value type by design.** `FlowKey` is embedded, not a pointer, so publishing is allocation-free on the hot path (benchmarked at 0 allocs/op per `plan/learned/1016-observation-feed.md`). Do not add pointer or slice fields to `Observation` without re-checking that guarantee.
- **Two of the four declared `Kind` values are never published today.** `observation.go:38-42` declares `KindInterface`, `KindSourceIP`, `KindDestIP`, `KindFlow`; only `KindSourceIP` (trafficusage) and `KindFlow` (flowexport) are ever constructed by a producer. `trafficstat.aggregator.ingest` (`internal/component/trafficstat/window.go:64-83`) has a live `case observation.KindDestIP` and a `case observation.KindInterface` (a no-op: interface rates are read from `iface.ListRates`, not the Feed) that no current publisher ever reaches. Do not assume `KindDestIP`/`KindInterface` observations exist in production; they are forward-declared, not dead-but-harmless.
- **Lazy, refcounted aggregators cost nothing when unattached.** `trafficfeature.Service` and `trafficstat.Service` only call `feed.Subscribe` on the 0->1 `Attach` transition and `feed.Unsubscribe` on the 1->0 `Detach` transition (`service.go:113-146`). Forgetting to `Detach` (e.g. a missing `defer`) leaks a permanent Feed subscription and a permanently running 1s tick goroutine.
- **Two unrelated fan-out mechanisms, easy to conflate.** The observation Feed (async, buffered, drop-on-full) and the iface `SubscribeCollectNotify` tick (synchronous, in-line, no buffer, `internal/component/iface/rate.go:240-244`) both use a copy-on-write subscriber list, but the iface one runs subscriber callbacks directly on the rate tracker's own ticker goroutine, a slow callback there delays every other subscriber's tick and the tracker's own metric update, unlike a slow Feed subscriber which only starves itself.
- **`SubscribeCollectNotify` is same-process only.** Both trafficusage and flowexport refuse to start as external plugin processes (`internal/plugins/trafficusage/register.go:67-68`, `internal/plugins/flowexport/register.go:107`) because the subscription is a plain Go function-pointer call into `internal/component/iface`'s package-level state; across a process boundary it would silently no-op with metrics staying empty and no error surfaced.
- **Cumulative vs delta semantics differ by producer.** trafficusage's eBPF byte counters are cumulative (`Observation.Value` is the raw counter); flowexport's conntrack flow bytes are deltas since the last dump. Consumers must not assume one convention feed-wide; `trafficfeature`/`trafficstat` route by `obs.Kind`/`obs.Feature`, not by a blanket cumulative-vs-delta flag.
- **Metric collection is always-on; only HTTP exposure is gated.** Without the `ze_telemetry` build tag, `metrics.StartExporter` stays `nil` (`exporter_hook.go:31`), so `registry.GetMetricsRegistry()` returns `nil` everywhere and every `BindMetrics`/`ConfigureMetrics` call is a no-op, components keep calling `Counter`/`Gauge` against nothing, no panics, but nothing is exported and no `/metrics` listener exists.
- **One registry, multiple owners, no second HTTP server.** The BGP reactor and the global plugin-injection slot (`registry.SetMetricsRegistry`) both receive the exact same `*metrics.PrometheusRegistry` instance from one `StartExporter` call (`internal/component/bgp/config/loader_create.go:202-205`); OS collectors, BGP metrics, and observation-feed metrics all land in that one registry and are served from the one `/metrics` handler.
- **gNMI does not export metrics or observations.** Despite living in this digest's scope, `gnmi.Get`/`Subscribe` read only the YANG config/state `Tree`; they are not wired to `observation.Feed`, `trafficfeature`, or the Prometheus registry beyond gNMI's own RPC counters. Do not assume enabling gNMI adds a streaming-telemetry path for `ze_*` metrics, it currently does not.
- **gNMI's per-path change notification is dormant.** `ChangeNotifier.NotifyChange` (`subscribe.go:89`) is implemented and unit-tested (`subscribe_test.go:90`) but has zero production callers; the only production path is the coarse `NotifyConfigReload` (`subscribe.go:78`), called once from `cmd/ze/hub/service_gnmi.go:134`, and `Set`'s own `notifySetResults` (`set.go:170`), which calls `Notify` directly with the raw gNMI `Update`/`Delete` rather than going through `NotifyChange`'s path-diffing helper. Do not assume a config change made outside a gNMI `Set` produces a granular per-path notification today, it produces one generic reload signal.
- **Counter-wrap protection is a repeated, not shared, convention.** `internal/component/telemetry/collector/delta_linux.go`'s `safeDelta`/`safeDeltaF64` and `internal/component/iface/rate.go`'s `rateDelta` independently implement the same "return 0 instead of a huge wrapped value when `cur < prev`" rule for uint64/uint32 kernel counters. There is no shared helper between the two packages; a new collector or rate computation must apply the check itself rather than assume it is inherited.
- **Cardinality cleanup is per-collector, not automatic.** Prometheus `GaugeVec`/`CounterVec` accumulate a stale label combination forever unless something calls `Delete()`. `netdev_linux.go` (interfaces) and `internal/component/iface/rate.go` (interfaces, again, independently) both track the previous tick's key set and delete labels for keys missing from the current tick; a new per-entity collector for a churning key space (tunnels, dynamic interfaces, ephemeral flows) must add the same tracking itself.
- **Telemetry config gating is layered, not a single flag.** The Prometheus HTTP exporter requires `telemetry.prometheus.enabled == "true"` with no implicit-enable (`exporter/server.go:244`); the nested Netdata OS-collector block defaults to enabled once the parent is (`exporter/server.go:355`) and can be independently disabled; individual collectors can be disabled or given a different interval via the YANG `collector` list (`internal/component/telemetry/collector/collector.go:95-97`). A collector silently producing no metrics is more likely a `collector` list override than a broken build.
- **Doc-vs-code drift.** `plan/learned/653-netdata-os-collectors.md` cites a metrics-package HTTP server file, since renamed and moved, that no longer exists at that path. Retired summary 386 carried the same dead path. The HTTP server logic moved to `internal/component/telemetry/exporter/server.go` behind the `ze_telemetry` gate as part of the compile-out seam (`exporter_hook.go`). `plan/learned/1016-observation-feed.md` also references a spec file that is not present in the current tree.
